questions.question: A number is first increased by 40% and then decreased by 25%, again increased by 15% and then decreased by 20%. What is the net increase/decrease per cent in the number?
questions.questionHtml: A number is first increased by 40% and then decreased by 25%, again increased by 15% and then decreased by 20%. What is the net increase/decrease per cent in the number?
questions.solution:
Given:

Number is first increased by 40% and then decreased by 25%, again increased by 15% and then decreased by 20%. 

Calculation:

Let the number be x

⇒ \({\rm{x\;}} \times \frac{{7}}{{5{\rm{\;}}}} \times \frac{{3}}{{4{\rm{\;}}}} \times \frac{{23}}{{20{\rm{\;}}}} \times \frac{{4}}{{5}}\)

⇒ \({\rm{x\;}} \times \frac{{483}}{{500{\rm{\;}}}}\)

⇒ 0.966x

⇒ 0.966x is less than x

⇒ Decrease per cent in the number = \(\frac{{{\rm{x}} - 0.996{\rm{x}}}}{{100}} = 3.4{\rm{\% \;}}\)

∴ Net decrease per cent in the number is 3.4%

questions.question: A person spends 75% of his income. If his income increases by 29% and his savings also increase by 20%, then the percentage increase in his expenditure is:
questions.questionHtml: A person spends 75% of his income. If his income increases by 29% and his savings also increase by 20%, then the percentage increase in his expenditure is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Initial Expenditure = 75%

Increase in income = 29%

Increase in savings = 20% 

Calculation:

Let the income be Rs. 100a.

Expenditure = 75% of 100a

⇒ Rs. 75a

Savings = 100a - 75a

⇒ Rs. 25a 

Increased income = 100a + 100 × 29%

⇒ Rs. 129a

Increase saving = 25a + 25a × 20%

⇒ Rs. 30a

So, new expenditure = 129a - 30a

⇒ 99a

Increase in expenditure = 99a - 75a = 24a

% of new expenditure = (24a/75a) × 100

⇒ 32

∴ The percentage increase in his expenditure is 32%.

questions.question: A shopkeeper gives 15% and 35% discounts on a bottle. If the selling price of the bottle is Rs. 1,547, then the marked price of the bottle is:
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper gives 15% and 35% discounts on a bottle. If the selling price of the bottle is Rs. 1,547, then the marked price of the bottle is:
questions.solution:
Given:-The given discount on the MRP of the bottle is 15% and 35%

To find:- The Marked price of the bottle

Formula used:- Selling price = Marked price × (100 - discount %)

Calculation:- Let the Marked price of the bottle be ' x ',

Total discount of 15% and 35% = 15 + 35 - \(\frac{15 \times 35}{100}\) = 50 - 5.25

Total discount = 44.75%

By using the formula,

Selling price = Marked price × (100% - discount %)

⇒SP = x × (100% - 44.75%)

⇒1547 = x × 55.25%

⇒x = \(\frac{1547\times 100}{55.25}\) = 2800

The marked price of the bottle is Rs 2,800.

questions.question: If the price of petrol increased by 7%, then by what percentage should the consumption be decreased by the consumer, if the expenditure on petrol remains unchanged?
questions.questionHtml: If the price of petrol increased by 7%, then by what percentage should the consumption be decreased by the consumer, if the expenditure on petrol remains unchanged?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If price increases by R%, reduction in consumption = [R ÷ (100 + R)] × 100%

Given, R = 7

⇒ Reduction % = [7 ÷ (100 + 7)] × 100%

⇒ Reduction % = (7 ÷ 107) × 100% = 700 ÷ 107 %

⇒ Reduction % = 6 58/107 %

∴ The correct answer is 6 58/107 %.

Alternate Method

Given:

Price increase of petrol = 7%

Formula Used:

Expenditure = Price × Consumption

Calculations:

⇒ Let original price = 100 units

⇒ New price after 7% increase = 100 + 7 = 107 units

⇒ To keep expenditure constant, the consumption ratio must be inversely proportional to the price ratio.

⇒ Ratio of Original Consumption to New Consumption = 107 : 100

⇒ Decrease in consumption = 107 − 100 = 7 units

⇒ Percentage decrease = (Decrease ÷ Original Consumption) × 100

⇒ Percentage decrease = (7 ÷ 107) × 100 = 700 ÷ 107 %

⇒ 700 ÷ 107 = 6 58/107 %

∴ The correct answer is 6 58/107 %.

Additional Information

Constant Expenditure Rule (Price Increase)

If the price of a commodity increases by R%, the percentage reduction in consumption required to keep the expenditure same is [R ÷ (100 + R)] × 100%.

Constant Expenditure Rule (Price Decrease)

If the price of a commodity decreases by R%, the percentage increase in consumption allowed to keep the expenditure same is [R ÷ (100 − R)] × 100%.

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes by A% and then by B%, the net percentage change is given by (A + B + AB ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: Ram spends 30% of his salary on food, 10% on house rent, 7% on entertainment, and 6% on conveyance. If at the end of a month his savings are ₹ 1,880, then his monthly salary is:
questions.questionHtml: Ram spends 30% of his salary on food, 10% on house rent, 7% on entertainment, and 6% on conveyance. If at the end of a month his savings are  ₹ 1,880, then his monthly salary is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Ram spends 30% of his salary on food, 10% on house rent, 7% on entertainment, and 6% on conveyance.

Savings at the end of the month = ₹1,880

Formula used:

Total percentage spent = 30% + 10% + 7% + 6%

Total percentage spent + Savings percentage = 100%

Calculation:

Total percentage spent = 30 + 10 + 7 + 6

⇒ Total percentage spent = 53%

Savings percentage = 100% - 53%

⇒ Savings percentage = 47%

Let the monthly salary be x.

Savings = 47% of x

⇒ 0.47x = 1880

⇒ x = 1880 / 0.47

⇒ x ≈ 4000

∴ The correct answer is option (4).

questions.question: The population of a certain village increases by 5 per cent annually. Its present population is 8200. After two year the population will be (approximately):
questions.questionHtml: The population of a certain village increases by 5 per cent annually. Its present population is 8200. After two year the population will be (approximately):
questions.solution:
Given :

Population increasing with the rate r = 5%

Current Population P0 = 8200

Time t = 2 years

Formula Used :

P = P0 (1 + r/100)t

Calculation :

Population after 2 years P = 8200 (1 + 5/100)2

⇒ P = 8200 × \(\frac{21 \times 21}{20 \times 20}\)

⇒ P = 9040.5 = 9040 (approx)

∴ The population of the village after 2 years = 9040 (approx).

questions.question: In an examination it is required to get a minimum of 340 marks in aggregate to pass. A student gets 244 marks and is declared failed by 12% of the total marks. What are the maximum aggregate marks a student can get?
questions.questionHtml: In an examination it is required to get a minimum of 340 marks in aggregate to pass. A student gets 244 marks and is declared failed by 12% of the total marks. What are the maximum aggregate marks a student can get?
questions.solution:
GIVEN:

Minimum marks required to pass = 340

CALCULATION:

Here, the minimum marks needed to pass = 340 marks 

⇒ A student secured = 244 marks 

⇒ Student failed by marks = Difference = ( 340 - 244 ) = 96 marks

But According to the given Question, a Student failed by 12% of the total marks 

⇒ 12% of the total marks = 96

⇒ 12/100 of the total marks = 96

⇒ Total marks = 96 × 100 /12 = 800

Hence, the maximum aggregate a student can get is 800.

questions.question: In a decade, a town's population grew from 1,75,000 to 2,62,500. What is the average annual percentage increase in population?
questions.questionHtml: In a decade, a town's population grew from 1,75,000 to 2,62,500. What is the average annual percentage increase in population?
questions.solution:
Given:

In a decade, a town's population grew from 1,75,000 to 2,62,500.

Formula used:

Percentage increase = \(\frac{\text {present value - old value}}{\text {old value}}\)

Average = \(\frac{\text {sum of all observations}}{\text {total number of observations}}\)

Calculation:

Percentage increase in a decade = \(\frac{262500-175000}{175000}\times 100=\frac{87500}{1750}=50\%\) 

Annual average = \(\frac{50}{10}=5\%\)

∴  The average annual percentage increase in population is 5%.

questions.question: By what percentage should a racer increase the speed to reduce the time by 25% to cover a fixed distance?
questions.questionHtml: By what percentage should a racer increase the speed to reduce the time by 25% to cover a fixed distance?
questions.solution:
Given:

Time reduction = 25%

Formula Used:

Speed ∝ 1 / Time

Percentage Increase in Speed = (New Speed - Old Speed) / Old Speed × 100%

Calculation:

Let the original speed be S and the original time be T.

New time = T - 0.25T = 0.75T

Since Speed ∝ 1 / Time:

New Speed = S / 0.75

New Speed = 4S / 3

Percentage Increase in Speed = ((4S / 3) - S) / S × 100%

⇒ Percentage Increase in Speed = (4/3 - 1) × 100%

⇒ Percentage Increase in Speed = (1/3) × 100%

⇒ Percentage Increase in Speed = 33 (1/3)%

The correct answer is option 4.

questions.question: Ramesh spends 60% of his income. If his income is increased by 30% and his expenditure is increased by 20%, then the percentage increase in the savings of Ramesh will be:
questions.questionHtml: <!-- x-tinymce/html -->Ramesh spends 60% of his income. If his income is increased by 30% and his expenditure is increased by 20%, then the percentage increase in the savings of Ramesh will be:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Expenditure to Savings = 60 : 40 = 3 : 2

Let the percentage increase in savings be x%.

Using the weighted average method for percentage change: (3 × 20 + 2 × x) ÷ (3 + 2) = 30

60 + 2x = 150 ⇒ 2x = 90

x = 45%

∴ The correct answer is 45%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ramesh spends 60% of his income.

His income increases by 30%.

His expenditure increases by 20%.

Formula Used:

Income = Expenditure + Savings

Percentage Increase = (Increase Value ÷ Initial Value) × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Let Ramesh's initial income be 100.

⇒ Initial expenditure = 60% of 100 = 60

⇒ Initial savings = Income − Expenditure = 100 − 60 = 40

⇒ New income = 100 + (30% of 100) = 130

⇒ New expenditure = 60 + (20% of 60) = 60 + 12 = 72

⇒ New savings = New income − New expenditure = 130 − 72 = 58

⇒ Increase in savings = 58 − 40 = 18

⇒ Percentage increase in savings = (Increase in savings ÷ Initial savings) × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = (18 ÷ 40) × 100 = 45%

∴ The correct answer is 45%.

Additional Information

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage change = [(Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100. A positive result indicates an increase, while a negative result implies a decrease.

Weighted Average Method

When a base value is split into two parts in the ratio m:n, and their respective percentage changes are a% and b%, the net percentage change is given by (ma + nb) ÷ (m + n).

Successive Percentage Change

If a value undergoes two successive percentage changes of a% and b%, the net percentage change is calculated as (a + b + ab ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: If each side of a rectangle is decreased by 11%, then its area will decrease by:
questions.questionHtml: If each side of a rectangle is decreased by 11%, then its area will decrease by:
questions.solution:
Given:

The length of a rectangle is decreased by 11%

The breadth of the rectangle is decreased by 11%

Formula used:

Area of rectangle = Length × Breadth

Calculation:

Let the length of the rectangle be L and breadth be B

The initial area of rectangle = LB

As the length of the rectangle is decreased by 11%

Decreased length = L – 11% of L

⇒ Decreased length = 0.89L

As, the breadth of the rectangle is decreased by 11%

Decreased breadth = B – 11% of B

⇒ Decreased Breadth = 0.89B

New area of rectangle = 0.89L × 0.89B

⇒ New area of the rectangle = 0.7921LB

Total decrease in area = LB – 0.7921LB = 0.2079LB

Percentage decrease in area = (Total decrease/Initial area) × 100

⇒ Percentage decrease in area = (0.2079LB/LB) × 100 = 20.79%

∴ The percentage decrease in the area is 20.79%

Shortcut Trick

Decrease in area = -x + (-y) + (-x)(-y)/100

∴ Decrease in area = -11 - 11 + 121/100 = -20.79%

⇒ 200X – 173X = 81000

⇒ 27X = 81000

⇒ X = 81000/27

⇒ X = 3000

∴ He originally had 3000 apples.

questions.question: Due to fall in manpower, the production in a company decreases by 35%. By what percentage should the working hours be increased to restore the original production?
questions.questionHtml: Due to fall in manpower, the production in a company decreases by 35%. By what percentage should the working hours be increased to restore the original production?
questions.solution:
Given:

Decrease in production of company = 35%

Concept Used:

Total Work = Manpower/Production × Working Hours

Calculation:

Let the total number of men be 100 and the working hours be 10 hours.

⇒ Total work = 100 × 10 = 1000 units

⇒ Men left after decrease = 100 – 35% of 100 = 100 – \(\frac{35}{100}\) × 100

⇒ Men left after decrease = 100 – 35 = 65

After the decrease, let the working hours be x.

Equating with the total work, we get

⇒ 65 × x = 10000

⇒ x = \(\frac{10000}{65}\) = 153.85 hours

⇒ Working hours should increase by percent = 153.85 – 100 = 53.85%

Therefore, the working hours should be increased by 53.85% to restore the original production.

questions.question: The population of a town is 80,000. It decreases by 8% in the first year and increases by 5% in the second year. What will be the population of the town at the end of 2 years?
questions.questionHtml: The population of a town is 80,000. It decreases by 8% in the first year and increases by 5% in the second year. What will be the population of the town at the end of 2 years?
questions.solution:
GIVEN:

Population = 80,000

population decreases in the 1st year = 8%

population increases in the 2nd year = 5%

FORMULA USED:

New value = ( 100 + X)/100 × Actual value , where X = percent by which value is increased.

New value = ( 100 - X)/100 × Actual value , where X = percent by which value is decreased.

CALCULATION:

Population of town after 1st year = 80,000 - 80,000 × 8 /100 = (80,000- 6,400) = 73,600

Population of town after 2nd year = 73,600 + 73,600 × 5/100 = ( 73,600 + 3,680) = 77,280

∴ The population at the end of 2 years is 77,280.

1932 units = 40 × 1932 = 77280

∴ The correct answer is 77280.

questions.question: A person saves 25% of his income. If his income increases by 20% and his saving remains the same, then what will be the increased percentage of his expenditure?
questions.questionHtml: A person saves 25% of his income. If his income increases by 20% and his saving remains the same, then what will be the increased percentage of his expenditure?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let initial Income = 100, which means Savings = 25 and Expenditure = 75.

New Income = 120 (increased by 20%) and Savings = 25 (remains constant).

New Expenditure = 120 − 25 = 95.

Increase in Expenditure = 95 − 75 = 20.

Percentage Increase = (20 ÷ 75) × 100 = 26 2/3%.

∴ The correct answer is 26 2/3%.

Alternate Method

Given:

A person saves 25% of his income.

Income increases by 20% while savings remain the same.

Formula Used:

Income = Expenditure + Savings

Percentage Increase = (Increase in Value ÷ Original Value) × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Let the initial income be 100 units.

⇒ Initial saving = 25% of 100 = 25 units

⇒ Initial expenditure = 100 − 25 = 75 units

⇒ After a 20% increase, the new income = 100 + 20% of 100 = 120 units

⇒ New saving = 25 units (as it remains the same)

⇒ New expenditure = 120 − 25 = 95 units

⇒ Increase in expenditure = 95 − 75 = 20 units

⇒ Percentage increase in expenditure = (20 ÷ 75) × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = (4 ÷ 15) × 100 = 80 ÷ 3 = 26 2/3%

∴ The correct answer is 26 2/3%.

Additional Information

Income-Expenditure Concept

The foundational equation is Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any change in income will exactly equal the sum of changes in expenditure and savings.

Constant Variable Effect

If savings remain constant, the entire absolute increase in income directly translates to the absolute increase in expenditure.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage change is always calculated based on the initial value: % Change = [(Final − Initial) ÷ Initial] × 100.

questions.question: The university has 750 faculty (male and female only) out of which the females are 60%. The average height of females is 162 cm and that of males is 168 cm. What is the average height of the faculty (in cm) of the university?
questions.questionHtml: The university has 750 faculty (male and female only) out of which the females are 60%. The average height of females is 162 cm and that of males is 168 cm. What is the average height of the faculty (in cm) of the university?
questions.solution:
Number of females = 0.60 × 750 = 450

Number of males = 750 - 450 = 300

Total height of females = 450 × 162 = 72900 cm

Total height of males = 300 × 168 = 50400 cm

Average height = (72900 + 50400) / 750 = 164.4 cm
